column1: Enable CDC in the current Azure SQL Database with {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db;}}
column2:
Requires db_owner and a supported tier: any vCore tier, or DTU S3 and higher. Enable source tables separately.
Review source

column1: After enabling CDC on the database, enable a source table through {{c1::sys.sp_cdc_enable_table}}.
column2:
Specify the source schema, table name, and gating-role choice.
Review source

column1: For capture instance dbo_Orders, CDC function {{c1::cdc.fn_cdc_get_all_changes_dbo_Orders}} reads changes between log sequence numbers (LSNs).
column2:
Use boundaries within the retained CDC validity window.
Review source

column1: To include before-and-after update rows in a CDC all-changes query, use row filter {{c1::'all update old'}}.
column2:
For updates, the 'all' filter returns only the after-update row.
Review source

column1: The CDC metadata column that identifies insert, update, and delete records is {{c1::__$operation}}.
column2:
Values 1 and 2 mean delete and insert. Values 3 and 4 identify before-update and after-update rows.
Review source

column1: Enable Change Tracking for YourDatabase with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE [YourDatabase] SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON;}}
column2:
Configure CHANGE_RETENTION and AUTO_CLEANUP to match the consumer's processing and recovery needs.
Review source

column1: After enabling database-level Change Tracking, track Orders with {{c1::ALTER TABLE dbo.Orders ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING;}}
column2:
Change Tracking must be enabled separately on each table that the function monitors.
Review source

column1: In isolated-worker C#, monitor Orders using {{c1::[SqlTrigger("[dbo].[Orders]", "SqlConnectionString")]}} on the batch parameter.
column2:
The parameter can have type IReadOnlyList<SqlChange<Order>>, where Order matches the table's row structure.
Review source

column1: With CES preview prerequisites met, enable streaming in the current user database through {{c1::sys.sp_enable_event_stream}}.
column2:
SQL Server 2025 requires full recovery and enabled PREVIEW_FEATURES. Creating a stream group is a separate step.
Review source

column1: Create a CES preview stream group through {{c1::sys.sp_create_event_stream_group}}.
column2:
This system procedure replaces the lesson's invalid CREATE EVENT STREAMING GROUP syntax.
Review source

column1: Add a table to a CES preview stream group through {{c1::sys.sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group}}.
column2:
Supply the stream group name and the schema-qualified table name.
Review source

column1: CES preview cannot be enabled in a database already enabled for {{c1::CDC}}.
column2:
The restriction applies at database level, not just to an individual table.
Review source

column1: CES preview publishes row-change events in the {{c1::CloudEvents}} format.
column2:
Payloads can include previous and new values, subject to data-type and size limits.
Review source
